audit_protocol_delta.reason: S18-S33 use the corrected paragraph protocol; defended content is not rewritten for cosmetic churn.

carry_forward_constraints: S34 must not consume S33 model metrics as valid promotion evidence unless dummy, rule and candidate were evaluated on the exact same held-out sample ids/folds and information set. S33's current handcrafted/disconnected metrics are not creditable.
The majority dummy must be fit only on training labels and then frozen. Never recompute class prevalence/majority from validation or test y before predicting; S33-F09 is a mandatory regression test.

S34 metric rows must be keyed to sample/pair ids with exactly one mature gold label and one prediction per eligible example. Validate binary label domain, target policy/version, prediction origin and horizon maturity before any precision/recall/F-score calculation.
Preserve S33's triage boundary: needs_review_* prioritizes human review and is not a fraud, crime, parentesco or culpability label. Metric names or thresholds must not reframe it as such.
Any S34 comparison must use the same FP/FN cost contract for dummy, rule and candidate. Beating dummy accuracy is not sufficient when a stronger rule baseline or lower-cost baseline exists.

S34 must receive a machine-valid S32 feature-set manifest and a fitted S33 Pipeline/estimator run manifest. Preprocessing must have been fit inside each training fold; no global imputer/scaler/vocabulary fit before CV is creditable.

For entity_pair rows, grouped validation must prevent either endpoint from appearing across train/validation when unseen-entity generalization is the estimand. A single group label per pair is insufficient unless its construction proves that invariant.

When time matters, every baseline and candidate must share the same prediction origin and information set. Do not reuse actual outcomes from inside the validation horizon as predictor inputs unless the protocol is explicitly rolling one-step for every method.

S34 introduces precision, recall, F-score, PR-AUC and top-k/capacity. Define each with numerator, denominator, positive class, support and edge cases before use; do not inherit S33's unexplained f1 metric as already learned.

Threshold selection, calibration and final evaluation must not reuse the same holdout for tuning and reporting. Use a train/validation(calibration/threshold)/test design or an equivalent nested/CV protocol and freeze the decision policy before final test.

Report prevalence and support alongside imbalance-sensitive metrics. Empty slices or zero-positive/zero-predicted-positive denominators must be handled explicitly rather than silently converted into performance claims.

Calibration in S34 means agreement between predicted probability and observed frequency, not generic weight/threshold tuning. Use out-of-sample probabilities and keep the distinction from S30/S33 score tuning.
Top-k/review-capacity metrics must use a declared eligible population, k/capacity and tie policy. Compare against frozen baselines under the same capacity constraint.
Error slices must be derived from actual prediction rows with support and provenance, not from hand-written indices or precomputed aggregate scores.
Keep the S33 temporal task switch quarantined: do not mix daily workload forecasting MAE with needs_review classification metrics in one promotion gate.

The model run must preserve feature_set/data/split/code/library/model identities, params/seed, baseline predictions, candidate predictions and costs; a run_id plus arbitrary metrics dict is insufficient lineage.

Keep real pytest regression gates for leaked dummy fitting, pair-endpoint fold overlap, preprocessing-fit leakage, target/horizon mismatch, label maturity, nonfinite probabilities, empty folds and unequal prediction/gold cardinality.
Inherited Level-2 and S29-S33 regression debt remains active. S34 cannot convert invalid upstream outputs into a green metric dashboard and call the workbench validated.
